And greetings from the cold and frozen northeast part of the country.
We're dipping down with wind chills to 20 to 30 degrees below zero this evening, so it's a cold one out there.
Our guest this week is Ron Olson from Laser Reflections, and his studio has been doing pulsed reflection holography of live subjects for a number of years.
They do absolutely gorgeous work, and Ron's going to come on to talk about uh his studio and some of the projects and also a book that he has coming up that he's uh writing on this topic.

Uh upcoming guests, uh we have Ron Kirk coming up in the next few weeks, and I've also received the holographic C D that has uh holographic uh music on it that we're going to get some samples from and uh talk about holographic sound as well.
That's another upcoming show.
Uh had a few strange workshops this week.

I had one gentleman come in for a workshop for laser pointer holography who is from one of the largest research corporations in the country, in fact, probably the world, and he had told his co-researchers about this guy in Allentown, Pennsylvania that was doing laser pointer holography, and they insisted that number one, I was nuts, that he was wasting his time, it wasn't possible.
And another researcher said yes theoretically it's just impossible to do it.
But uh he came in, made a beautiful reflection hologram, and he's going back to his labs on Monday to show them that.
Also, another uh young man who came in to take a workshop from New England.
He drove down.
It was a nine-hour drive, but he was doing it for his senior research project.
And uh I'll tell you something, his professor told him straight out that it was impossible to do holograms using a laser pointer or a laser diode, and uh they were pretty adamant about it.

And uh he was listening, he's been a listener to the Holo Talk Show for uh quite a long time, and he says, Frank, if you say that it can be done, I know it can be done, so I'm coming down to take a workshop.
Can I come down and make a hologram?
And he left today.
In fact, uh he left around 1 30, 2 o'clock this afternoon, and it's a little after 8 in the evening, so he's not even home yet.
He's got a long drive, and uh he's taking a really nice uh hologram back of a Lamborghini that he did using a laser pointer.
So there's a few people that are in for surprises on Monday when they find out that yes, it is possible to do holography using one of the laser pointers.
I got a few holograms in from Ronnie Andresen.
I think I'm pronouncing that name pretty close to being correct from Norway, and I want to tell you folks, his holograms are absolutely gorgeous.

So he said, Frank, I'm gonna send you a few, and I was really looking forward to looking at them.

When I opened that box up and I put those holograms under the light, my jaw hit the table.
I could not believe how gorgeous, absolutely gorgeous these holograms were using the $7.90 the $7.99 laser pointer.
Just absolutely incredible.

This this baby's been running around the clock and it only shuts down for a minute or two at a time.

But we're just going to let that run tonight because it's so cold I don't even want to turn that off for a little bit.

Yeah.

Yes.

Mm-hmm.

Uh the studio's in its third location now we went from Felton to San Jose and now we're in downtown San Francisco.

Which was a shame.

Yeah, yeah.

Uh good holography for for commercial holography to survive requires a fair investment of capital.
We have about three hundred thousand dollars into our imaging system here at Laser Reflections.
And uh that's that's with uh with a lot of uh kind of uh surplus government parts.
If I Bernadette and I are also partners in a laser company, Positive Light, which we started about the same time uh we started Laser Reflections, Positive Light makes high energy lasers.
But it costs me more to buy uh uh a laser today that with my own company uh than it did uh twenty years ago.

I think between for the small laser it might be s somewhere closer to sixty and for the large one uh something around a hundred thousand dollars.

This is that for two people in in a studio, this is what Bernadette and I can do.

This is did we get the right image, not did we get the uh you know did the laser fire.

Mm-hmm exactly.

It sure will be.
Okay.

How did you land that?

Wow.

But this is not the case anymore.

Uh this is not just at Stanford and Harvard and you know, Penn State these days.
This is you can go in onto any college campus in this country and find high energy lasers at work.
And as they these kids get trained, they as they come out of school, they're they're very adept laser operators.

For holography it really hasn't changed.
The holography, the the the light requirements for doing single color holography like we do have not changed.
The hardware package is basically the same.
So as many sciences, obsolete lasers like ours, they become available in a secondary market.
So now you have the combination of skilled trained laser operators at the university level and second hand equipment coming available on the market for pennies on the dollar.
This then makes for for studios like ours to be a reality.

This is what we at Laser Reflections are going to look to do, is to build a number of studios around the country uh where we can hire trained laser operators who will then we hope have uh great careers in holography.
Well Ron, do you have any closing comments or any remarks you'd like to make to the listeners before we uh head out here?
No, just uh if you if and when they're in San Francisco uh to come and visit our studio.
We're right down we're a block from the uh Museum of Modern Art and two blocks from the Moscone Center.
Okay.
Ron, I want to thank you very much for taking the time.
I know you have to be very busy for uh coming on the show.
Well you're most welcome friend.
If you get a chance log on and listen to it.
We'll do for sure.
Okay.
All right thank you very much for welcome.
Right bye bye
